LESSON: CREATIVE WRITING

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: GERMAN
Strand: Writing 3.1 Guided Writing (Vocabulary) (1 session) By the end of the sub- stran
Topic 3.7: Creative writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Creative writing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Which is the hardest part of writing in a foreign language?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify elements of creative writing in a given text
2. write entertaining and informative texts in varied contexts
3. appreciate the role of creativity in writing

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: CREATIVE WRITING
Subject: GERMAN · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Creative writing helps you succeed in GERMAN. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: CREATIVE WRITING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify elements of creative writing in a given text

What this means
In this part you learn to identify elements of creative writing in a given text. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify elements of creative writing in a given text.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Creative writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify elements of creative writing in a given text. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Write entertaining and informative texts in varied contexts

What this means
In this part you learn to write entertaining and informative texts in varied contexts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write entertaining and informative texts in varied contexts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Creative writing to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write entertaining and informative texts in varied contexts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the role of creativity in writing

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of creativity in writing. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of creativity in writing.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of creativity in writing. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Creative writing is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Creative writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify elements of creative writing in a given text)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Creative writing to a partner. (skill: write entertaining and informative texts in varied contexts)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the role of creativity in writing)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Creative writing to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify elements of creative writing in a given text.
3. Practise this skill: write entertaining and informative texts in varied contexts.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the role of creativity in writing.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Creative writing from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Creative writing: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Creative writing?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Which is the hardest part of writing in a foreign language?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Creative writing means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify elements of creative writing in a given text.
5. Be able to: write entertaining and informative texts in varied contexts.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
